content.text: Incomplete aortic valve closure -> LV vol overload w eventual LV dilation & HF
: congenital bicuspid valve; calcific valve dz; prior endocarditis; aortic root dilation – Marfan syndrome, inflam disorders, rheumatic fever, syphilis, HTN
severe dyspnea, pulm edema, acute HF
PE: hyperdynamic apical pulse displaced to Lt
swift upstroke & rapid fall of radial pulse accentuated w wrist elevation
systolic or diasoltic thrill/murmur over femoral arteries
•↑ venous return: squat, supine, leg raise
Austin-Flint Murmur (severe): mid-late diastolic rumble @ apex 2/2 retrograde regurgitant jet competing w antegrade flow from LA into LV
: acute or Sx, aSx w LV decompensation (EF <55%)
: retrograde blood flow from pulmonary artery into RV → R-sided volume overload
No tx needed in most (well tolerated)
Blood backs up into the right atrium → increased right atrial enlargement → right sided HF
•opening snap (usually later than snap of MS)
: commissurotomy or replacement if R-HF or ↓ CO
•obstruction of flow from LA to LV secondary to narrowed mitral orifice → blood backs up into the left atrium
rheumatic heart disease almost always the cause
•congenital, left atrial myxoma, thrombus, valvulitis (SLE, amyloid, carcinoid)
best tx for symptomatic MS in younger pts
w/ noncalcified valves or if refractory to medical therapy
: reserved if mitral valvuloplasty is contraindicated or w/ unfavorable valve morphology
•diuretics & sodium restriction for edema & volume overload
•rate control of AFIB w/ BBs, CCBs, or digoxin (anticoag. for AFIB – warfarin)
